_notes: Oracle for Stage C (BLUEPRINT 5.3) on four scripted answers. Stage C's input is (transcript, target competency, the question's why), so run it with each answer's `context`: the JD file, the target competency resolved through expected_rubric_hints.json (the entry of that JD whose match_keywords contain competency_match_keyword), the question text, ladder_rung and strategy, and the jd_keywords list handed to the prompt. Without that context the keyword and evidence expectations are meaningless.

Synthesise each script with Kokoro to wav_file, run STT, then Stage C. word_count is the script's whitespace token count and must NOT be asserted against the STT transcript. spoken_word_count_approx estimates what TTS actually says (digits become number words, all-caps abbreviations are spelled out, hyphen compounds are two words; the rule is verify_fixtures.spoken_word_count) and is the number to use for WPM sanity checks. approx_duration_s is spoken_word_count_approx at 155 wpm; recompute the real duration from the WAV before asserting timestamp containment.

quote_substrings, the star.*.quote_substrings, hedges_quote_substrings and overlapping_quotes_both_valid are exact substrings of the SCRIPT and each occurs exactly once in it, so a timestamp-containment test has one unambiguous span per quote. At least one quote_substrings entry must fuzzy-match (RapidFuzz partial_ratio >= 90 on normalised text) a quote the analyzer returns. Digits and abbreviations are kept out of quotes because STT may spell them out.

Under LM Studio's strict json_schema (all properties required, additionalProperties false) every property is emitted: an absent STAR part arrives as {"present": false, "quote": null, "t": null}. Assert `part.get("quote") in (None, "")`, never key absence. star.action.ownership_any_of lists the acceptable values of the action's ownership field; the prompt's enum is I | we | unclear, and the quote gate may relabel it from pronoun counts.

ownership_ratio_hint counts first-person singular (I, my) versus plural (we, our) tokens in the script; we_ratio = we / (I + we); team_hiding_flag = we_ratio > 0.7 (the 5.3 heuristic) and is always a boolean. Only sample_answer_team trips it. The vague answer sits at 0.67 on purpose: it is the borderline case the threshold must NOT flag.

jd_keyword_hits_any_of and jd_keyword_missed_any_of are subsets of context.jd_keywords; every listed hit occurs as a whole word (or hyphenated phrase) in the script and every listed miss does not. Assert the analyzer's hit list contains at least one of hits_any_of and its missed list at least one of missed_any_of; when jd_keyword_hits_expected_empty is true the hit list must be empty. Keyword matching is token based: 'TTL' is deliberately not a JD keyword because it only matches jd_fintech.txt through 'se-ttl-ements'; it lives in evidence_keywords_any_of, which matches the competency's evidence, not the JD.

evidence_updates_expected constrains the target competency's cells after this answer. evidence_updates may arrive as a dict keyed by competency id (the BLUEPRINT shape) or as a list of {competency_id, evidence, level} objects; normalise both before asserting. any_level: at least one cell is at that level. max_level: no cell is above that level (none < weak < strong).
contradictions_expected_empty: these are single-turn fixtures with no prior claims, so contradictions must be [].

overlapping_quotes_both_valid (vague only): both quotes must survive the quote gate with overlapping t ranges; the gate must not reject a quote because another validated quote already covers part of the same words.
verdict_any_of, next_strategy_any_of and reaction_any_of are the acceptable sets from the enums in 5.2 / 5.3. specificity_min / specificity_max bound the 0-3 score.
